title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: CURTIS'S LADDER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Curtis Boyle, a furnace repairman from Wichita, Kansas.
He can fix any heater in the state. But he had not spoken to his brother Dale in eleven years. All because of a ladder.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE LADDER
segments.quote: A man that studieth revenge keeps his own wounds green.
segments.author: Francis Bacon
lines: Dale borrowed his best ladder and never brought it back. Curtis told that story to every customer, while they sat there cold.
Then a card came. Mom was turning eighty, and both boys had better show up.
Old Mrs. Ortega heard the ladder story and opened her Francis Bacon:
A man that studieth revenge keeps his own wounds green.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE MATH
segments.quote: How much more grievous are the consequences of anger than the causes of it.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: That night, he did the math. One ladder, one hundred eighty-nine dollars.
Eleven years, two weddings, a nephew he had never met.
His wife Renee read him a line from Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor:
How much more grievous are the consequences of anger than the causes of it.
Curtis looked at the bill. He had overpaid.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: MOM'S KITCHEN
segments.quote: I can forgive, but I cannot forget, is only another way of saying, I will not forgive.
segments.author: Henry Ward Beecher
lines: He went to see Mom. I can forgive him, he said. But I won't forget that ladder.
She kept peeling potatoes. Henry Ward Beecher, the old American speaker, beat you to that:
I can forgive, but I cannot forget, is only another way of saying, I will not forgive.
Then she wrote Dale's number on a paper towel.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE CALL
segments.quote: To forgive is to set a prisoner free and discover that the prisoner was you.
segments.author: Lewis B. Smedes
lines: The paper towel rode on his dashboard for nine days.
Tito at the supply house kept a line from the writer Lewis Smedes over the register:
To forgive is to set a prisoner free and discover that the prisoner was you.
Curtis sat in the truck and dialed. A long quiet. Then Dale said, is this about the ladder?

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE TARP
segments.author: Harry S. Truman
lines: Saturday, Curtis moved an old tarp behind his shed. There it was. His ladder.
A faded note was taped to it, in Dale's writing. Thanks, bro.
Curtis sat down on a paint can. His dad's old Harry Truman sign hung on the garage wall:
The buck stops here.
He drove to Salina with that ladder and said, Dale, it was me. Dale laughed until he had to sit down.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TABLE
segments.quote: The family, that dear octopus from whose tentacles we never quite escape, nor, in our inmost hearts, ever quite wish to.
segments.author: Dodie Smith
lines: At Mom's party, there were forty folding chairs and one very shy nephew.
Mom raised her iced tea, and read from the English writer Dodie Smith:
The family, that dear octopus from whose tentacles we never quite escape, nor, in our inmost hearts, ever quite wish to.
Now the brothers clean her gutters every fall. They still argue about who holds the ladder.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Let it heal. Count the cost. Forgive. Pick up the phone. Own it. Go home.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: Let it heal. Count the cost. Really forgive. Pick up the phone. Own your part. Go home.
My own brother still has my good umbrella. It might be in my closet.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
